Rings when a call you set up is due.
Set up a simulated incoming call that looks natural when you need a way out. You stay in control of when it appears.
Offline only: your profiles and schedules stay in app-private storage. The app does not connect to a server or send analytics.
Simulation only: caller profiles are fictional display details used only inside this app.
No real calls: AlibiCall does not dial numbers, spoof caller ID, access contacts or call logs, or impersonate real people or organisations.

Every call is simulated on this phone. Nobody is dialled and no audio is connected. The call screens do not say so, so that the call looks natural.
Your call settings could not be saved. Please try again.
Pick the one that matches the Phone app on your phone, then preview it. These are look-alikes and may differ in small details.
Google Phone (default on many OnePlus phones)
When on, the call fills the screen, also over the lock screen, showing the caller name. When off, it appears as a notification.
Android is blocking full-screen notifications for AlibiCall.
Press volume down 5 times within 3 seconds. One short buzz confirms it, and the call rings after your delay. Two buzzes mean it could not be set up.

To turn it on, enable AlibiCall in Android Accessibility settings. The service only looks at volume-down presses. It cannot read your screen, it stores no key history and nothing leaves your phone. The volume still changes as usual. It generally works only while the screen is on. Turn it off there at any time.
If Android says the setting is restricted (apps installed from a file): open Settings, Apps, AlibiCall, the three-dot menu, then Allow restricted settings.
Starts your simulated call when you press volume down 5 times quickly. Only volume-down presses are checked. Screen content is not read and nothing is sent anywhere.
Choose a delay from 1 second to 120 minutes.
